clue.text: It was golden in Colchis

parts.note: the clue recalls the Greek myth of Jason and the Argonauts, who sailed to Colchis to seize a ram's golden coat

explanation.surface: A line of classical lore about something precious in the ancient kingdom of Colchis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Golden Fleece, the woolly coat of a winged ram, hung in a grove in Colchis until Jason took it.

clue.text: Bishop's seat in food stall collapses

indicators.note: the stall collapsing means the letters of food stall fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A church chair turns up among the wreckage of a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: A faldstool is a folding stool used by a bishop in a church not his own, or a prayer desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A faldstool is a portable folding chair used by a bishop at the altar.

clue.text: Right inside, but in the passage

indicators.note: inside places the letter for right within the word for but

parts.note: but means except, as in all but one

explanation.surface: A remark that something is correct within, yet stuck in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken from a book, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Its branches hold out the light

definitions.text: Its branches hold out the light

parts.words: Its branches hold out the light
parts.note: reads like a tree whose boughs block the sun, but the branches hold candles up

explanation.surface: A leafy tree's limbs keep the sunshine off.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabra is a branched candlestick, its arms holding lights out from the centre.

clue.text: Annoy to make one rattier

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the letters given are worked into something new, so 'to make' asks for them to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Annoying someone is a way of making them crosser, or rattier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is the anagram signal: I (one) plus RATTIER are rearranged. The surface is itself a fair joke, since annoying a person does make them rattier.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate someone is to annoy or vex them.

clue.text: Tried once to become abstruse

indicators.note: to become says the letters of tried once change into something else

explanation.surface: Something attempted only one time turns out baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means obscure, little known and hard to understand.

clue.text: Not very extensive island

definitions.meaning: in Scotland and Ireland an ... is a small island

explanation.surface: A small island, perhaps somewhere remote.
explanation.definitionFit: The short measure and the Gaelic-derived word for an islet share one spelling.

clue.text: Do away with a' queen for having rings

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or abolish
the letter given as written
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Abolish a queen in exchange for some jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular means ring-shaped or marked with rings, from the Latin for a little ring.

clue.text: Fat, solid girl is a non-starter

indicators.note: a non-starter loses its start, so the girl's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Hester is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A plump, sturdy girl has no chance of success.
explanation.walkthrough: Fats are esters of glycerol and fatty acids that are solid at room temperature, oils being the liquid ones; 'Fat' alone is just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemically a solid fat is a kind of ester, a compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: National tax

definitions.meaning: a native of one of the nations of Britain, someone from north of the border
an old levy or payment, surviving in the phrase meaning unpunished

explanation.surface: A levy imposed across the whole country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highlander is a national of Scotland, and scot was a medieval tax, hence getting off scot-free.

clue.text: Swindle layabout, say, using few words

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for lay is placed around the swindle

parts.note: lay, as in a lay person, not of the clergy, is LAIC
a swindle is a con

explanation.surface: Someone cheats an idle loafer while barely saying a word.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'layabout' does two jobs and has to be split: 'lay' is the piece and 'about' is the container signal. The word 'say' tells you lay is being given in another form, the old adjective for non-clerical.
explanation.definitionFit: A laconic speaker is terse, saying little, a word from the clipped speech of the Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: Shy feature concerns teachers

parts.note: a concern is a business, abbreviated CO for company, and two of them give CO twice
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A timid characteristic is said to worry schoolteachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' is not timid: a coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls to knock coconuts off posts. The plural 'concerns' gives two COs.
explanation.definitionFit: The prize and target at a coconut shy is the hairy nut itself, so it is the stall's main feature.

clue.text: Such verses are tortuous

definitions.meaning: a poetic term for a line that begins and ends with the same word, coiling back on itself
tortuous means winding, twisting like a snake

explanation.surface: A remark that certain kinds of poetry are hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the snake: verse that loops back to its opening word, and a course that winds and twists.

clue.text: A god with wings

parts.note: a lar is one of the Lares, Roman household gods

explanation.surface: A winged deity, like Mercury or Cupid.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lares were the guardian spirits of a Roman home; LAR is the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: Alar is a botanical and zoological adjective meaning winged or relating to wings.

clue.text: Expert's hypothesis upsets excellent record

definitions.note: read as expert is, the 's standing for is

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a hypothesis or guess

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsets means the word for excellent is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 read as the letter I
a list is a written record

explanation.surface: An expert's theory overturns a brilliant set of results.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist is someone with deep knowledge of one field, an authority.

clue.text: Where in France great riots resulted in violence

parts.note: the French for where is où

indicators.note: the word great runs riot, its letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Somewhere in France, huge riots ended in bloodshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riots' looks like part of the story but tells you to rearrange GREAT, giving TRAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is an act of gross violence or brutality.

clue.text: Nobility in drawing of the face

definitions.meaning: loftiness or grandeur of mind or style
an architect's flat drawing of one face of a building

explanation.surface: A noble quality shows in a portrait sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face' suggests a portrait, but it is the face of a building, as in facade.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation means exaltation or dignity, and in architecture a scale drawing of a building's front or side.

clue.text: I'm getting drinks from abroad, say

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for goods brought in from other countries

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
port is a fortified wine, so drinks gives ports

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of buying alcohol from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Port wine comes from Portugal, so the drinks are themselves an example of what the definition describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Imports are goods brought in from overseas, the 'say' warning that foreign drinks are only one example.

clue.text: It is covered up in neatest material

annotationWithheld.why: It is covered up in neatest material (9): the only parse puts IT reversed (up) inside an anagram of NEATEST, but no clue word signals that anagram unless 'material' is both indicator and definition
annotationWithheld.clue: It is covered up in neatest material

clue.text: Lake plant

definitions.meaning: a large Swiss lake beside the city of the same name
a fodder crop also called alfalfa

explanation.surface: Two terse words that could label a garden pond.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss lake and city share the name with alfalfa, a clover-like forage legume grown for cattle.

clue.text: College includes nude entertainment

indicators.note: includes says the college holds the word for nude inside it

parts.note: a CAT was a College of Advanced Technology in Britain
nude means bare

explanation.surface: A college puts naked performers in its show.
explanation.walkthrough: CAT, a British College of Advanced Technology, was a type of higher-education college of the 1950s and 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a show of songs, dancing or comedy staged in a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: "Bid me discourse, I will thine ear" (Venus and Adonis)

definitions.text: "Bid me discourse, I will thine ear" (Venus and Adonis)

parts.words: "Bid me discourse, I will thine ear" (Venus and Adonis)
parts.note: the missing verb completes Venus's promise to charm Adonis by her talk, a line from Shakespeare's poem

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's narrative poem with a word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus promises to captivate or bewitch the listener's hearing with her words.

clue.text: Fruit insect flying about for food

indicators.note: flying about pictures the insect circling the fruit, so it goes around it

parts.note: an ant is an insect
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A bug buzzes around a piece of fruit looking for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliment is an old word for nourishment or sustenance.

clue.text: Reminder about second class power

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reminder wraps around the letter for second class

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder
B is the grade or class after A

explanation.surface: A note goes round about the second-rate electricity supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power' is mathematical: the third power of a number is its cube.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a number raised to the third power is its cube.

clue.text: Medallion arrived with ring

parts.note: came means arrived
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A medal turned up together with a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a carved gem or medallion with a raised head in profile.

clue.text: Point beyond which no solution is possible

definitions.text: Point beyond which no solution is possible

parts.words: Point beyond which no solution is possible
parts.note: read as a problem with no answer, but in chemistry it is the stage where a liquid can dissolve no more

explanation.surface: A hopeless dilemma where nothing can be resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry the point where a solvent holds all the dissolved substance it can is its saturation point.

clue.text: One who insults missing sailor's employer

indicators.note: missing says the sailor is taken away from the word for one who insults

parts.note: an abuser hurls insults
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone abusive lacks the shipowner's employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' is not a boss: it is one who employs, or uses, something.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs a tool or method, putting it to use.

clue.text: Issue note for this number

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Publish a written note about this figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a piece of music, as in a band's next number.
explanation.definitionFit: A number in music is a song or piece performed.

clue.text: Physicist needs a drink — one available inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for available goes within the drink followed by one

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape pressings
one is the Roman numeral I
on means available, as in on offer

explanation.surface: A scientist wants a drink and there is one to hand indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Guglielmo Marconi, the Italian radio pioneer, won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1909.
explanation.definitionFit: Marconi shared the 1909 Nobel physics prize for his work on wireless telegraphy.

clue.text: Outstanding points in oriental plant

parts.note: oriental means eastern, abbreviated E

indicators.note: in places the compass points within the herb

parts.note: mint is a herb
N and E are compass points

explanation.surface: Notable features found on an Eastern plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent person is distinguished, standing out above others.

clue.text: Such figures can't go so out of shape

indicators.note: out of shape says the letters of can't go so are bent into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Some shapes refuse to be bent like that.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CANTGOSO gives eight-sided figures, and the clue is fitting since bending a shape is what an anagram does.
explanation.definitionFit: Octagons are plane figures with eight sides.

clue.text: Figure of a girl in rags? On the contrary

indicators.note: in would put the girl within the rags, but the closing words flip that
on the contrary says the containment is the other way round, the rags going inside the girl

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
tat is shabby cloth or rags

explanation.surface: A doll or effigy of a girl dressed in tatters, or is it the reverse?
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, the girl goes inside the rags. 'On the contrary' turns that round, so the rags sit inside the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure.
